sourceIssues.locator: Theorem A(ii), published p.4, and Theorem 3.16(ii), published p.55, author-hosted journal PDF; corresponding arXiv 1801.00872v3 / Wittenberg-manuscript pp.4,48.
sourceIssues.correction: For the even-genus equivalence in part (ii), add dim(X) ≥ 2 or X(R) = ∅. A simpler sufficient restriction is dim(X) ≥ 2. In the excluded case dim(X)=1 with X(R) nonempty, Pic descent is always surjective and the equivalence holds precisely when X itself has even genus. This finding does not require restricting part (i).
sourceIssues.reason: Use the smooth projective completion E of y²=x³−x over R. The cubic discriminant is 4 (Weierstrass discriminant 64); the point [0:1:0] is real and nonsingular, and E is geometrically integral of genus 1. Coherent H²(E,O_E)=0. Since E(C) is connected, H⁰_G(E(C),Z)=Z, generated by the codimension-zero cycle class [E]; hence the real integral Hodge conjecture for 1-cycles holds. The only reduced geometrically irreducible closed curve in E is E, so no even-genus curve exists. A real point splits Br(R)→Br(E); the low-degree Hochschild–Serre sequence therefore gives Pic(E)≅Pic(E_C)^G and hence the same isomorphism on 2-primary torsion. For the repair, Proposition 3.9 supplies even-genus curves when dim(X)≥2 and X(R)≠∅. If X(R)=∅, Theorems 3.3/3.6 apply without that dimension restriction; for curves this is exactly Lemma 3.7.

sourceIssues.locator: §2.2, constant-class paragraph before Example 2.5, published pp.37–38; arXiv 1801.00872v3 / Wittenberg-manuscript p.33.
sourceIssues.reason: For X=Spec R and k=0, the zeroth cup power is 1 in H⁰_G(pt,Z)=Z. It is not torsion and is the algebraic class of X, so it satisfies Definition 1.19 although X(R) is nonempty. Indeed for k=0 the only possible component is degree zero and Sq⁰ is the identity. For positive even k, ω^{2k} is 2-torsion. If X(R) is nonempty, its degree-zero component under §1.2.5 is 1, contradicting the requirement α₀=Sq^{−k}(α_k)=0 in Definition 1.19; if X(R) is empty the topological condition is vacuous. Thus k>0 even is exactly the intended range.

sourceIssues.locator: §2.2, explanatory prose immediately after (2.1), published p.37; arXiv 1801.00872v3 / Wittenberg-manuscript p.32.
sourceIssues.correction: The ambient group of the classes satisfying both conditions is H^{2k}_G(X(C),Z(k)); restore the subscript G in this prose occurrence.
sourceIssues.reason: The immediately preceding equality defines Hdg^{2k}_G(X(C),Z(k))₀ as an intersection of two subgroups of equivariant cohomology. The topological condition of Definition 1.19 uses equivariant restriction and is not a condition on an ordinary cohomology class alone. The forgetful map to ordinary cohomology is used only for the Hodge condition. The displayed equality and map (2.1) already use the correct ambient group.
